title: Test episodic agent rotation and learn the context break-even point
observation: Operator proposed replacing context-heavy long-running workers with fresh task-scoped workers that receive only required context and structured prior-stage state. This may avoid repeated history processing, but worker bootstrap, handoff, coordination, and rediscovery create a competing cost that must be measured.
suspected_root_cause: Long-lived workers can repeatedly reprocess stale context; current orchestration does not yet estimate when continuity costs more than starting a fresh episode with targeted retrieval and a structured handoff.
suggested_direction: Benchmark persistent workers against semantic-boundary rotation, model continuation and rotation cost explicitly, add an observable context-pressure score and shadow rotation advisor, and promote automatic rotation only after it lowers total cost per validated completion.
acceptance: A deterministic or replayable benchmark compares persistent-worker and fresh-worker strategies on identical objectives and validators
Measurements include worker bootstrap, handoff, targeted retrieval, rediscovery, retries, reviews, total tokens, latency, and validated result
Rotation-frequency experiments identify a diminishing-return or break-even region for at least one task family
A shadow rotation advisor can explain continue/compact/rotate/split recommendations without changing execution
Structured handoffs preserve artifacts, decisions, state, evidence, and source pointers
Recursive delegation depth/fan-out is bounded and measured
Automatic rotation is enabled only after noninferior validation and improved total cost per successful task
risks: Over-rotation can make bootstrap and coordination cost exceed context savings
Over-compressed handoffs can create rediscovery, errors, and repair loops
Excessive recursive delegation can replace temporal context amplification with branch/fan-out amplification

source.reference: 2026-09-29 request to test fresh subagent rotation for context/token efficiency

notes: High priority, shadow/measurement first. Integrate with IMP-0018 telemetry rather than creating a parallel measurement stack.
